note: TypeScript modules under app/ that no page reaches, as of the day scripts/check-reachable.mjs landed (2026-08-22). The filing law says a file kept 'just in case' is a file the next person has to evaluate, and unreferenced code is the quiet kind: it compiles, it passes every other gate, and it reads like working code. Each entry names an owner, because deleting a module or wiring it back in is the owner's call and this gate edits nothing. This list is meant to SHRINK. Anything not on it fails the gate.

allowed.why: renders the whole staff dashboard from loadFixtures(), and no page loads it — b-dashboard/index.html names staff-dashboard.js instead, which is hand-written JavaScript with no TypeScript source (see sources-baseline.json). Two modules for one dashboard, and the compiled one is the one nothing runs. Which of the two is the real dashboard is Manny's call

loadFixtures(), the one shared fixture loader the data law names. Its only importer is b-dashboard/main.ts, which no page loads, so nothing the site serves reads app/shared/fixtures.json. check-fixtures.mjs still validates that file against the contract and still prints its staleness countdown, which is worth keeping — but read the countdown as being about records, not about a screen: no screen shows them. Whether the legacy loader has a future is a team question, not a lane one

the pulse mark as a callable, documented in components/README.md as one of the three shared pieces. Nothing imports it: every header draws its own mark. Either a page should use it or the README should stop promising it
